long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Jacob Hilfiger entered fashion through retail rather than formal design school. As a teenager in Elmira, New York, he bought bell-bottom jeans in Manhattan and resold them locally before opening People's Place. The store eventually failed, but the experience clarified his interest in clothing design. After moving to New York City, he worked with businessman Mohan Murjani to introduce a menswear collection under his own name in 1985.

Hilfiger refreshed button-down shirts, chinos and other American staples with relaxed proportions, then linked the label to music, celebrity and youth culture. The combination turned a menswear line into a broader apparel and licensed-lifestyle business. Private-equity firm Apax acquired the company in 2006, and PVH purchased it four years later as a major global brand. Hilfiger remained through both ownership changes. He now serves as principal designer, setting creative direction while PVH owns and operates the commercial platform. His lasting contribution is a distinctive version of accessible American sportswear built as much through cultural positioning as through product design.
